mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW X5 40i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full BMW X5 40i engine replacement typically costs £3,800-£6,800 supply-only for a rebuilt B58 unit, or £4,500-£7,500 fitted by a specialist. Used engines start from £2,000, while reconditioned units typically cost £3,200-£5,000. Prices vary by exact B58 variant (B58B30C / B58B30M1 / B58B30P). Professional fitting adds £800-£1,200 to any engine purchase. Rebuilt units include upgraded cooling and gasket components. 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty on all rebuilt engines.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW X5 40i reliable? How long does the B58 engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B58 is widely considered BMW's most reliable modern petrol engine. The closed-deck design and proven architecture mean B58 engines regularly exceed 150,000-200,000 miles with proper maintenance. Annual oil changes (not BMW's extended intervals) are critical. Coolant system components (expansion tank, water pump) are the main wear items. B58 is significantly more reliable than the N55 it replaced. Many specialists report B58s reaching 200,000+ miles with preventative maintenance.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the BMW X5 40i B58 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B58B30 family has three well-documented failure points: coolant system leaks (expansion tank, water pump), oil filter housing gasket leaks (burning oil smell), and high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure. All three typically appear between 30,000-100,000 miles. Coolant expansion tank replacement at specialist: £300-£500. Water pump replacement at specialist: £500-£800. Oil filter housing gasket at specialist: £300-£500. HPFP replacement at specialist: £800-£1,200. Catch issues early to avoid full engine replacement. B58 coolant system components can fail without warning - check coolant levels monthly.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a BMW X5 40i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2019-2024 X5 40i worth £18,000-£45,000, a £3,800-£6,800 rebuilt B58 engine represents excellent value - typically 10-20% of the vehicle's value. The decision depends on the individual car's condition and your ownership horizon. Replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value on most examples. If body and gearbox are sound, a rebuilt engine adds years of life. Used engine (£2,000-£3,500) is the budget option. Rebuilt engine (£3,800-£6,800) offers warranty and peace of mind. B58 engines rarely need full replacement - repairs usually suffice.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW X5 40i and the xDrive40i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 40i badge refers to the engine - the B58 3.0-litre turbocharged petrol straight-six. xDrive is BMW's all-wheel-drive system. In the UK, all X5 40i models are xDrive (all-wheel drive). In North America, a rear-wheel-drive sDrive40i variant was also available. 40i = engine designation (B58 3.0L turbo petrol). xDrive = all-wheel drive (UK market standard). sDrive = rear-wheel drive (North America only). All UK X5 40i models are xDrive40i.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my BMW X5 40i engine with a different size or fuel type?

acceptedAnswer.text: Engine swaps to a different size or fuel type are technically complex and rarely cost-effective on the G05 X5. Stick to like-for-like replacement using the correct B58 engine code (B58B30C, B58B30M1, or B58B30P) for your X5 40i. ECU, wiring loom, fuel system, and exhaust all differ between petrol and diesel. Mild hybrid (48V) components are engine-specific. Insurance must be notified of any non-standard engine swap. Specialist marketplace only recommends like-for-like code-matching for warranty coverage.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW X5 40i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW X5 40i was introduced with the fourth-generation G05 X5 in 2018, replacing the previous F15-generation xDrive35i. Powered by the B58 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six petrol engine - widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable modern powerplants - the 40i became the entry-level petrol model in the G05 range, offered in both rear-wheel-drive sDrive40i (North America) and all-wheel-drive xDrive40i (UK and global) configurations.

milestones.description: B58B30C, 3.0L turbocharged petrol, 340hp - launch engine for G05 X5 xDrive40i
B58B30M1, 3.0L turbocharged petrol, 340hp - updated engine calibration with revised emissions compliance
Mild hybrid (48V) system introduced across B58B30M1, adding electric torque assistance and improved fuel economy
B58B30P, 3.0L turbocharged petrol with 48V mild hybrid, 375hp - G05 LCI facelift power increase
xDrive50e PHEV launched alongside, but 40i remains the core petrol entry model

commonProblems.h2: BMW X5 40i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW X5 40i is powered exclusively by the B58B30 family - a 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six petrol engine widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable modern powerplants. The B58 features a closed-deck engine block design, which significantly improves strength and durability compared to its N55 predecessor. While the B58 is a robust engine, it has several well-documented minor failure points that become more common as mileage climbs past 60,000 miles. Rebuilt B58 engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Coolant System Failure - Why the BMW X5 40i Loses Coolant and Overheats
problems.rootCause: The B58 engine uses a plastic coolant expansion tank and integrated supply lines that can develop hairline cracks under thermal cycling. The water pump and thermostat housing are also common leak points. Coolant loss, if ignored, can lead to overheating and potential head gasket failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace coolant expansion tank and supply line, bleed cooling system
repairOptions.longevity: 30,000-60,000 miles. Viable if low coolant warning appears but no overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric water pump, thermostat, and coolant
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000-80,000 miles. Recommended preventatively on B58 engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt B58 engine with updated cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if overheating caused head gasket or block damage (rare on B58).

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2019-2024 BMW X5 40i is valued at approximately £18,000-£45,000 in the UK market. With a rebuilt B58 engine costing £3,800-£6,800 supply-only (plus £800-£1,200 fitting), replacement cost represents 10-20% of vehicle value on most examples - making full replacement highly viable for all but the oldest, highest-mileage examples.
problems.recommendation: The B58's coolant system is the primary weak point, but it rarely causes catastrophic failure if addressed promptly. For under £500 at a specialist, expansion tank replacement is cheap insurance. On any X5 40i approaching 60,000 miles, consider preventative water pump replacement. The B58 is BMW's most reliable modern petrol engine - full replacement is rarely needed unless the engine has been driven after overheating.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B58 BMW X5 40i engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Filter Housing Gasket Leaks - Why the BMW X5 40i Smells of Burning Oil
problems.rootCause: The oil filter housing gasket degrades over time due to heat cycling, allowing oil to seep onto the exhaust manifold. This causes a burning oil smell and, if ignored, can lead to oil starvation and alternator damage from oil contamination.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Oil filter housing gasket replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace oil filter housing gasket, clean oil residue, top up oil
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000-100,000 miles. Viable if caught early - no secondary damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt B58 engine with new gaskets throughout, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation caused bearing damage (very rare on B58).

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See above. Specialist gasket replacement under £500 is cost-effective on any X5 40i.
problems.recommendation: The oil filter housing gasket leak is one of the most common B58 issues - and one of the cheapest to fix if caught early. Check for oil residue around the oil filter housing at every service. If you smell burning oil after a drive, have the gasket inspected immediately - the repair is under £500 at a specialist and prevents much more expensive engine damage.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B58 BMW X5 40i engine prices

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure - Why the BMW X5 40i Won't Start
problems.rootCause: The high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) in the B58 engine delivers fuel at the required pressure for optimal combustion. Over time, internal wear can cause the HPFP to fail, leading to hard starting, engine stalling, and a noticeable drop in power.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace high-pressure fuel pump, flush fuel system
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000-100,000 miles. Viable if caught before secondary damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt B58 engine with new HPFP, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if HPFP failure caused fuel contamination or engine damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See above. Specialist HPFP replacement under £1,200 is cost-effective on any X5 40i worth more than £8,000.
problems.recommendation: HPFP failure on the B58 is less common than on earlier BMW turbo engines (N54/N55), but it does occur. Symptoms include hard starting and loss of power under acceleration. If the Check Engine Light illuminates with fuel pressure-related codes, have the HPFP inspected immediately. Catastrophic failure is rare, but a failing pump can contaminate the fuel system with metal particles.
